title: Impact of Iodinated Contrast Media on Renal and Thyroid Parameters: A Retrospective Analysis Following Implementation of new Contrast Media Guidelines at Heidelberg University Hospital
summary: Contrast-enhanced CT examinations are routinely performed in hospitals. The iodinated contrast agent used can affect renal and thyroid parameters. To prevent organ damage, guidelines define laboratory thresholds (elevated creatinine, reduced TSH) at which protective measures should be initiated. At Heidelberg University Hospital, these thresholds were substantially lowered. The aim of this retrospective study is to assess whether this lowering has a positive, neutral, or negative impact on patient safety and relevant clinical outcomes. For this purpose, the patient database at Heidelberg will be analyzed.
conditions: Contrast-associated acute kidney injury (AKI) and deterioration of renal function, as well as iodine-induced thyroid dysfunction (especially hyperthyroidism/thyrotoxicosis up to thyrotoxic crisis) in the context of contrast-enhanced CT.

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of all patients at Heidelberg University Hospital who underwent contrast-enhanced CT with intravenous iodinated contrast during 07/2021–06/2023. Pseudonymized routine data are extracted from hospital and radiology information systems (via the Medical Data Integration Center):

Same data collection for 07/2023–06/2025 after implementation of the updated contrast SOP. Cohort comparison and within-window pre/post changes are assessed. Repeated CT examinations per patient are handled appropriately (e.g., patient-level clustering or aggregation).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Examination using iodinated contrast media.
Exclusion criteria:
No examination using iodinated contrast media.
